questions.question: The primary function of the resume is to serve as:
options: The official legal record of employment
A marketing tool to obtain an interview
A guarantee of obtaining the desired job
A comprehensive biography of the applicant

questions.question: The initial amount of time an employer takes to review an applicant’s resume is typically:
options: Several minutes if the applicant is highly qualified
Only enough time to check for abbreviations

questions.question: All of the following information should be included in the Header section of a resume EXCEPT:
If a student's calculated GPA is 3.062, the advice given for presenting this GPA on a resume is to:
options: Round down to the nearest tenth (3.0)
Only include it if it is 4.0

questions.question: When describing responsibilities for a past job that the applicant is no longer employed at, the responsibilities section should use:
Which of the following is considered a Resume 'Don't'?
options: Keeping the resume easy to read
Including personal pronouns such as I, me, or my
Keeping the resume about one page long

questions.question: The goal of technical writing, first and foremost, is to:
options: Employ rich imagery or powerful metaphors
Communicate complex information clearly and precisely

questions.question: Technical writing is considered a fundamental skill for anyone working in science and engineering because it is necessary for documents like progress reports, proposals, CVs, and graduation projects.
According to the Ladder of Abstraction, as one moves up the ladder, the definition of a technical component becomes:

A measure of how well a technical writer has written a document includes assessing both how well the reader understands the intended meaning AND how well that understanding fulfills the intended purpose or need at hand.
Technical writing relies heavily on visuals (pictures, graphs, tables, etc.) because they are used by the writer to:
options: Clarify, explain, and support an idea

questions.question: Which characteristic of technical writing dictates that conclusions and judgments must be based on evidence or established expertise, and supported by facts, laws, and references?
Ethics in technical writing involves a writer's moral duty and obligation to apply communication power to the purpose of doing worthy things.
A technical writer must not substitute speculation for facts, hide the truth with ambiguity, or inject personal bias into their report.
Which type of plagiarism occurs when a writer uses a previously published or submitted paper for a new project (e.g., submitting the same research paper for two courses) without permission?
If you paraphrase an author's ideas very well in your own words but fail to provide a citation, this is primarily categorized as:
To correctly avoid plagiarism when using an author's exact words, the writer must show the original words in quotation marks and provide a citation.
If a digital image used in a technical report has been fundamentally changed (altered) to represent different information, the ethical requirement is to:
options: Acknowledge the alteration in the caption and briefly describe its nature
Use it without citation since you modified it

questions.question: A document that is appealing, well-addressed to its audience, but is unethical, will still put the reader at a disadvantage by:
options: Not allowing him/her to make the best decision

questions.question: The ethical model for technical writers includes the principles of:
In the technical definition structure (Term = Classification + Differentiation), the role of the Classification is to:
options: Narrow the meaning to one possibility
Place the term into a general category
Explain the theory behind the term

questions.question: If the term being defined has more than one meaning (e.g., 'stall'), the writer should add a Qualifier (such as 'In driving...') to the definition statement to:
Defining a 10kΩ resistor as an 'electrical device that impedes the flow of electric current' is problematic because the classification 'electrical device' is:
When writing for a non-technical audience, a writer may need to sacrifice desired precision to communicate effectively, which is known as:
Which definition extension should be used if the writer needs to trace the linguistic history or origin of a term?
Which definition extension should be used if the writer wants to organize related technical concepts into specific categories?
If you define 'zeolite' as an 'exchange resin' but suspect your audience doesn't know what an 'exchange resin' is, you should use the Further Definition extension to clarify the nested term.
The use of an analogy like 'Zeolite collects calcium and magnesium ions in the same way a feather broom collects dust' is an example of which extension type?
Differentiation is the part of the definition process that narrows the meaning of the term to just one possibility within the chosen general class.
Which extension type would be appropriate for explaining why a negatively charged element attracts positively charged ions?
Mechanism descriptions typically focus on an object in space and detail its:
Process descriptions are precise portrayals of events that occur:
options: Over time and lead to some outcome

questions.question: The general organizational structure for both Mechanism and Process descriptions includes Introduction, Discussion, and Conclusions.
When discussing the parts of a mechanism, ordering them spatially could involve arranging them:
options: From left to right or inside out

questions.question: The main difference in the use of visuals between mechanism and process descriptions is that process visuals usually need to show:
options: Movement through space and time (e.g., with arrows)

questions.question: In a Mechanism Description, the Introduction section must include a technical definition of the mechanism and an overall description of the mechanism's function or purpose.
When describing a conceptual process (like an algorithm), the Discussion section focuses primarily on:
options: Defining the step and describing its function or purpose

questions.question: When using compound numbering for visuals in a report (e.g., Fig. 3.2), the number '3' indicates the:
What is the fundamental purpose of a proposal document?
options: To prove expertise in a subject
To offer persuasive solutions to problems and request support (usually money)
To criticize previous attempts to solve the problem

questions.question: An assembly line worker sending a supervisor a letter suggesting a change to a manufacturing process is an example of a(n):
A Solicited Proposal is one that:
options: Has a high chance of being accepted
Is written by a team of experts
Responds to a specific request, where the problem has already been identified
Is written only when the recipient does not realize a problem exists

questions.question: Formal proposals are often divided into five volumes. Which volume contains the detailed analysis and data regarding the financial requirements of the project?
In a Formal Proposal, the Management volume is where the writer describes:
options: The engineering details of the solution
The organizational structure and key players who will implement the proposal

questions.question: The Executive Summary is highly critical because it:
options: Is typically written by the HR team
Is often the only part of the proposal that senior decision-makers read
Provides the final breakdown of resources
Is usually only one page long

questions.question: The Cover Letter or Transmittal Letter accompanying a proposal:
options: Acts as a substitute for the title page
Is considered an essential part of the formal proposal's table of contents
Ensures the proposal is considered in the proper context and gets to the right person
Should contain the detailed background of the problem

questions.question: In the Costs section of an Informal Proposal, it is specifically advised to avoid:
options: Only putting a single big final cost

questions.question: Feasibility and Recommendation Reports are both objective documents that define a problem and evaluate solutions based on a set of criteria.
Which of the following describes the key difference in scope between Feasibility and Recommendation Reports?
options: Feasibility reports use data; Recommendation reports use interpretations
Feasibility reports consider a single solution; Recommendation reports look at several approaches
Feasibility reports are biased; Recommendation reports are objective
Recommendation reports require an appendix; Feasibility reports do not

questions.question: Progress reports that mark movement toward a final goal on large projects are sometimes known as:
When writing a Progress Report, the overall assessment section should include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: An appraisal of the current status
A forecast for completing the project
A detailed description of the original problem only
An assessment of the progress made to date

questions.question: When detailing tasks completed in a Progress Report, you must describe the things accomplished, the difficulties encountered, and:
options: The final cost of the project
How long it took to accomplish them
The original purpose of the report

questions.question: In a standard Laboratory Report, the Materials and Procedure section must be written using:
The standard Lab Report structure includes Data, which consists of quantitative (numerical) data, qualitative (non-numerical) data, and drawings.
The Conclusion section of a Feasibility Report must review the data and interpretations, present conclusions based on that data, and:
options: Recommend or reject the proposed solution
Discuss future work not treated in the report

questions.question: In the context of a Research Paper, the Abstract should typically be limited to:
options: Not more than half a page
As long as necessary to cover all results

questions.question: The recommended practice for writing a research paper is the 'Inside out writing' approach, which suggests that the writer should fill in the Body of the paper first, and write the Abstract last.
Which section of a research paper or thesis is located at the end of the Introduction and describes the contents of the body chapters?
options: Outline of the rest of the paper

questions.question: Which characteristic makes a thesis or dissertation 'Poor'?
According to the source, to be listed as an author on a paper, an individual must have:
options: Only made a significant intellectual contribution
Only contributed to drafting or revising
Made a significant intellectual contribution, contributed to drafting/revising, and approved the final version

questions.question: The primary purpose of the Literature Review chapter in a thesis is to:
options: Detail the materials and methods used
Review relevant literature and identify gaps in current knowledge
